subStrands.name: Pre-Islamic Arabia, Prophet Muhammad, Rightly-Guided Caliphs and Islam in West Africa

objectives.description: The Jahiliyyah — Arabia before Islam: description of Arabia (location, social life, marriage, divorce and inheritance, religious life — idol worship and names of major gods, political life, economic life); the reforms introduced by Islam on the Jahiliyyah practices.

The life of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.): birth; marriage; call to prophethood and his mission; Hijrah — causes, course and significance; formation of the Ummah and the Madinan Constitution; leadership qualities; the Battles of Badr, Uhud and Khandaq; Treaty of Hudaybiyyah; Conquest of Makkah; Farewell Pilgrimage; death.
The Khulafā'ur-Rāshidīn (Rightly-Guided Caliphs): Abu-Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthmān and 'Ali — biographies, contributions to Islam, lessons learnt.

Islam in West Africa: advent and roles of traders, teachers, murābitun, sufi orders, mujaddidun and Hajj in the spread of Islam; impact of Islam on the socio-political, economic and linguistic lives of the peoples of ancient West African empires (Ghana, Mali, Shonghai and Kanem-Borno).

subStrands.name: Revelation, Preservation, Importance and Selected Suwar

objectives.description: Revelation of the Qur'an: visits of the Prophet to Cave Hira; first revelation and reaction; different modes of revelation; piecemeal revelation.
Preservation of the Qur'an: complete arrangement including distinction between Makki and Madani Suwar; recording; compilation; standardization; roles played by the Companions.
Importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance in social, political, spiritual and moral matters.

Reading, memorization, meaning and lessons from selected Suwar: Suratul Fatihah (Q.1), Suratud Duha (Q.93), Suratut Tin (Q.95), Suratul 'Alaq (Q.96:1-5), Suratul Qadr (Q.97), Suratul Kafirun (Q.109), Suratun Nasr (Q.110), Suratul Ikhlas (Q.112), Suratul Falaq (Q.113), Suratun Nas (Q.114).
Moral lessons from the Qur'an: attitudes to parents (Q.17:23-24; 31:13-15); honesty in words and deeds (Q.2:42; 61:2-3; 17:35); prohibition of gambling (Q.2:219; 5:90-91).

Definition of Hadith and Sunnah; differences and similarities between Hadith and Sunnah; importance of Hadith and Sunnah; parts of the Hadith ('Isnad, Matn and Rawi); criteria for authenticity; classification — Sahih, Hasan and Da'if; the Six Sound Collections of Hadith (Sihaus-Sittah) and their compilers.
Reading, memorization, meaning and lessons from selected Ahadith: an-Nawawi's Collection nos. 1, 5, 7, 9, 13, 15, 16, 18, 34 and 41.

strands.name: Tawhid and Fiqh (Islamic Theology and Jurisprudence)

subStrands.name: Faith, Prayer, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj and Islamic Ethics

objectives.description: 'Iman (Faith): meaning and significance; Articles of Faith — belief in Allah with emphasis on Kalimatush-Shahadah (Q.2:163, 255; 3:18; 17:42-43; 21:22; 23:91; Q.112), Islam and Trinity (Q.4:171; 5:75-76); His angels (Q.2:285; 8:50; 16:2; 66:6; 82:10-12); His books (Q.2:2; 2:285; 87:19); His Prophets with special emphasis on Ulu'l-'Azm: Ibrahim, Nuh, Musa, 'Isa, Muhammad.
Salah (Prayer): meaning, purpose and importance; conditions and prerequisites (taharah — wudu and ghusl); times and raka'ahs; Salat al-Jumu'ah, Salat al-Janazah, Salat al-'Idain.
Zakah (Obligatory Almsgiving): meaning; importance; nisab and hawl; people entitled to receive zakah (Q.9:60); differences between zakah and sadaqah.
Sawm (Fasting): meaning; importance; types; rules and regulations; Laylat al-Qadr; Zakatul-Fitr — meaning and purpose.
Hajj (Pilgrimage): meaning; importance; conditions; pillars of Hajj; rites and their significance; types — Ifrad, Qiran, Tamattu'; distinction from 'Umrah.

Islamic ethics: concept of 'Amanah (trustworthiness), 'Adalah (justice), Ihsan (excellence), Tawadu (humility), Sabr (patience), Shura (consultation); prohibition of shirk, kibr (pride), hasad (envy), ghiba (backbiting) and namimah (tale-bearing).
